candidates.name: ModEightEscape
candidates.title: Collatz: escape to 5 or 7 modulo 8
candidates.summary: Every positive ordinary Collatz trajectory eventually reaches $1$ or a number congruent to $5$ or $7$ modulo $8$.
candidates.statement: For every $n>0$, there is $k\ge0$ such that $C^k(n)=1$, $C^k(n)\equiv5\pmod8$, or $C^k(n)\equiv7\pmod8$.
scope: This is Yolcu–Aaronson–Heule Conjecture 4.14, expressed without a nonconvergence premise.
A trajectory may reach one of the two residue classes and continue indefinitely. The question does not require every start to reach 1.
The October 2026 formalized weakenings add an extra residue class; this statement has no extra exit.
candidates.example: $C(3)=10$ and $C^2(3)=5$, so $n=3$ has an exit at step $2$. The start $n=7$ has an exit at time zero.

conventions.detail: $C(n)=n/2$ for even $n$, and $C(n)=3n+1$ for odd $n$. Time zero is allowed.

candidates.difficulty: The exact modulo-8 avoidance problem survives recent formalized one-residue weakenings and documented limits of finite termination certificates. Those weaker theorems do not remove their extra exit.
candidates.openness: Named open conjecture, with explicit October 2, 2026 primary-source frontier. No proof of the exact endpoint found in this bounded screen.

references.label: Yolcu–Aaronson–Heule, §4.5, Conjecture 4.14; ordinary map defined in §1
Nashida, October 2, 2026, modulo-8 weakenings and certificate barriers

candidates.name: SqrtPassageGaussian
candidates.title: Collatz: Gaussian fluctuations of square-root descent
candidates.summary: Over all starts $1\le n\le N$, the first shortcut passage below $\sqrt n$, centered at $\log n/\log(4/3)$ and scaled by $\sqrt{(\log3)^2\log n/(\log(4/3))^3}$, has a standard normal limit.
candidates.statement: Put $d=\log(4/3)$ and $b_z(n)=\log n/d+z\sqrt{(\log3)^2\log n/d^3}$. For every real $z$, the proportion of $1\le n\le N$ whose first shortcut passage to a value at most $\sqrt n$ occurs by time $b_z(n)$ tends to the standard normal cumulative probability $\Phi(z)$.
scope: This review packet proposes the exact square-root first-passage CLT as a new research formulation motivated by published stochastic models. It is not a named published conjecture, and no priority claim is made.
The denominator is N, including starts with no finite passage. No convergence to 1 is assumed.
The known coarse trajectory concentration does not establish this square-root-of-logarithm fluctuation scale.

Full Collatz asserts eventual arrival at 1, without this quantitative distribution. This question stops at square-root descent; no implication in either direction between the full Collatz conjecture and this precise limit is claimed.
candidates.example: The shortcut trajectory $16,8,4$ first reaches $\sqrt{16}=4$ at step $2$. A later visit does not count as the first passage.

conventions.detail: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$; all logarithms are natural.
The exact condition is $(T^k(n))^2\le n$ and $(T^j(n))^2>n$ for all $j<k$.

candidates.difficulty: Typical passage takes about 3.476 log n steps, beyond the initial parity uniformity window of about 1.443 log n. A central limit theorem requires sqrt(log n) precision, whereas Inselmann's comparison permits epsilon log n errors. The published density-one transport estimates do not preserve events of intermediate limiting density Phi(z), so they do not directly transport the proposed Gaussian law.
candidates.openness: Proposed exact formulation: no deterministic integer-start first-passage CLT with this normalization found. Absence-of-proof screen is bounded, not a certification of exhaustive novelty.

references.label: Inselmann, Theorems 1.1 and 1.3: coarse natural-density trajectory approximation
September 2026 Gaussian history law: a different total-variation word cutoff

provenance.motivation: Kontorovich–Lagarias stochastic first passage; deterministic comparison with Inselmann
provenance.logical_relation_to_full_collatz: No implication/equivalence or strict hardness ordering established. It measures a prefix ending at sqrt(n), not convergence to 1.

candidates.name: ExponentialSyracuseMixing
candidates.title: Collatz: exponential fine-scale Syracuse mixing
candidates.summary: The exact Syracuse offset law modulo $3^n$ approaches the uniform lift of its coarse law modulo $3^m$ with $L^1$ error at most $C e^{-cm}$, uniformly for $1\le m\le n$.
candidates.statement: Let $p_n$ be the exact rational Syracuse offset mass defined below. Are there constants $C,c>0$ such that, for every $1\le m\le n$, $\sum_{r=0}^{3^n-1}|p_n(r)-3^{m-n}p_m(r\bmod3^m)|\le C e^{-cm}$?
scope: The coarse law is not uniform: it assigns zero mass to multiples of 3.
This strengthens the superpolynomial mixing estimate in Tao's Proposition 1.14 to the exponential rate predicted in Remark 1.15.
It is an analytic subproblem about a precisely defined probability law. It asserts no universal convergence of integer Collatz trajectories.
The September 2026 retained-weight mixing theorem was compared in full: its conductor is the exponent of 3 and its bound is an arbitrary fixed inverse power, not the exponential rate asked here.
candidates.example: Modulo $3$, the masses at $0,1,2$ are $0,1/3,2/3$. When $m=n$, the displayed error is zero.

conventions.detail: At level n+1, send a residue y to $(3y+1)2^{-a}$ modulo $3^{n+1}$, with the geometric law of a summed over its period $L=2\cdot3^n$. The exact weight is $2^{L-a}/(2^L-1)$ for $1\le a\le L$.
The displayed L1 sum is twice the usual total variation distance; the existential constant C absorbs that factor.

candidates.difficulty: A bound by every fixed inverse power does not supply uniform exponential decay; the constants may depend on the power. The target asks for one pair C,c valid at all scales.
candidates.openness: Tao v7 (July 16, 2026), Remark 1.15 predicts this exponential strengthening. The September 2026 preprint was read in full: Theorem 5.2, equation (63), still proves only O_A(m^(-A)) for each fixed A, and section 9 assumes its analytic estimates in Lean. No exact proof or unconditional formalization was located in the bounded current screen.

references.label: Tao, v7 (July 16, 2026), Lemma 1.12, equation (1.23), Proposition 1.14 and Remark 1.15
al-Jammas–Kolpakov–Luo, Theorem 5.2 (63), conductor convention §2 and Lean scope §9: inverse-power estimate only
